summary: Space Agency Simulator is a Unity WebGL game about running a space program. Players assemble rockets, choose missions, and balance budget, public mood, and long-term upgrades while a persistent clock advances days and triggers government funding. Live NASA content daily astronomy images, Earth imagery from EPIC, gives each session a real-world connection. The project tackles the challenge of making a management sim approachable without sacrificing depth: it runs instantly in the browser, guides new players through a short tutorial, and keeps the interface familiar while adding economy, progression, and mission-risk systems. It matters because it turns spaceflight operations into an accessible, replayable experience and shows how public scientific data can enrich a game.
details: We developed SpaceAgency Simulator, an interactive management and engineering game where players build and run their own space agency from the ground up. Players have to balance tight budgets, maintain public approval, and construct custom rockets from 50 handcrafted parts. To ground the simulation in real-world space exploration, the game also features an in-game NASA Mission Briefing (accessible via F1 or the pause menu) that pulls live Earth imagery from NASA’s EPIC camera and daily Near-Earth Object tracking data from NeoWs. Spaceflight often feels distant and overly complex, so our goal was to make aerospace engineering and the real financial trade-offs of rocket launches approachable, educational, and fun for players of all ages. Built over a 48-hour hackathon sprint where our team simply skipped sleep to bring this vision to life across three laptops, we combined custom 3D models, pixel art, and engaging simulation mechanics using Unity, Visual Studio Code, Blender, Pixilart.com, and Gemini. What makes our project truly creative is its cohesive execution—blending space travel into a polished, playable experience.
